claim: Mycobacterium tuberculosis is the leading worldwide cause of death due to a single infectious agent.
source: Mycobacterium tuberculosis is the leading worldwide cause of death due to a single infectious agent.
evidence: This is a statement of fact about TB mortality presented in the abstract.

claim: Existing anti-tuberculous therapies require long treatments and are complicated by multi-drug-resistant strains.
source: Existing anti-tuberculous therapies require long treatments and are complicated by multi-drug-resistant strains.
evidence: This is a general statement about TB treatment challenges supported by established knowledge in the field.

claim: The zebrafish-Mycobacterium marinum infection model can be used as a whole-animal screening platform to identify FDA-approved, host-directed compounds.
source: Here, we use the zebrafish-Mycobacterium marinum infection model as a whole-animal screening platform to identify FDA-approved, host-directed compounds.
evidence: The manuscript describes the actual use of this model for screening, supported by the experimental data presented.

claim: Multiple compounds that modulate host immunity to limit mycobacterial disease were identified, including clemastine.
source: We identify multiple compounds that modulate host immunity to limit mycobacterial disease, including the inexpensive, safe, and widely used drug clemastine.
evidence: This is supported by the screening data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Clemastine is inexpensive, safe, and widely used.
source: We identify multiple compounds that modulate host immunity to limit mycobacterial disease, including the inexpensive, safe, and widely used drug clemastine.
evidence: This is a statement about the known properties of clemastine as an FDA-approved drug.

claim: Clemastine alters macrophage calcium transients through potentiation of the purinergic receptor P2RX7.
source: We find that clemastine alters macrophage calcium transients through potentiation of the purinergic receptor P2RX7.
evidence: This is supported by the calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 3 and Videos 2-4.

claim: Host-directed drug activity in zebrafish larvae depends on both P2RX7 and inflammasome signaling.
source: Host-directed drug activity in zebrafish larvae depends on both P2RX7 and inflammasome signaling.
evidence: This is supported by experiments with p2rx7 mutants (Figure 4) and asc mutants (Figure 5).

claim: Clemastine is effective within the complex granulomas that are the hallmark of mycobacterial infection.
source: Using a novel explant model, we find that clemastine is also effective within the complex granulomas that are the hallmark of mycobacterial infection.
evidence: This is supported by the granuloma explant experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Tuberculosis killed approximately 1.6 million people in 2017, with around 10 million new active cases.
source: Tuberculosis killed approximately 1.6 million people in 2017, with around 10 million new active cases (World Health Organization, 2018).
evidence: This is cited from the World Health Organization 2018 report.

claim: Current tuberculosis treatment requires at least 6 months of treatment with multiple antibiotics.
source: The continued difficulty in treatment arises, in large part, from long and relatively complex treatment regimens, currently requiring at least 6 months of treatment with multiple antibiotics (World Health Organization, 2018).
evidence: This is cited from the World Health Organization 2018 report.

claim: Failures in treatment and poor patient adherence have driven the emergence of drug-resistant strains.
source: Failures in treatment and poor patient adherence have driven the emergence of drug-resistant strains that present further therapeutic and public health challenges.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about TB drug resistance.

claim: Host-directed therapies are designed to enhance host-mediated clearance of bacteria or limit immunopathology rather than targeting bacterial processes directly.
source: Host-directed therapies (HDTs) are a new conceptual approach designed to enhance host-mediated clearance of bacteria or limit immunopathology rather than targeting bacterial processes directly (Clatworthy et al., 2018; Hawn et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from Clatworthy et al., 2018 and Hawn et al., 2013.

claim: Host-directed therapies avoid the danger of commonly arising bacterial mutations that eliminate binding of the drug to a bacterial target.
source: Notably, they avoid the danger of commonly arising bacterial mutations that eliminate binding of the drug to a bacterial target.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the advantage of HDTs based on their mechanism of action.

claim: Few potential host-directed therapies for tuberculosis have advanced to clinical trials.
source: Although a number of potential HDTs for tuberculosis (TB) have been identified in cell-culture-based models and directed animal studies, few have advanced to clinical trials (Clatworthy et al., 2018; Hawn et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from Clatworthy et al., 2018 and Hawn et al., 2013.

claim: Mycobacterium marinum is one of the closest relatives of the Mtb complex.
source: Zebrafish are natural hosts of Mycobacterium marinum, one of the closest relatives of the Mtb complex (Tobin and Ramakrishnan, 2008).
evidence: This is cited from Tobin and Ramakrishnan, 2008.

claim: M. marinum and Mtb share conserved virulence loci and induce similar host immune responses and pathology, including the formation of granulomas.
source: M. marinum and Mtb share conserved virulence loci and induce similar host immune responses and pathology, including the formation of granulomas (Davis et al., 2002).
evidence: This is cited from Davis et al., 2002.

claim: Genes identified in zebrafish as determinants of mycobacterial disease progression have also been associated with disease severity and outcome in humans.
source: Genes identified in zebrafish as determinants of mycobacterial disease progression have also been associated with disease severity and outcome in humans (Thuong et al., 2017; Tobin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from Thuong et al., 2017 and Tobin et al., 2012.

claim: Zebrafish larvae are optically transparent, allowing both pathogen and host processes to be imaged in vivo in a natural host.
source: Because zebrafish larvae are optically transparent, both pathogen and host processes can be imaged in vivo in a natural host.
evidence: This is a known property of zebrafish larvae used in research.

claim: M. marinum infection of larval zebrafish recapitulates key aspects of tuberculosis pathogenesis.
source: M. marinum infection of larval zebrafish recapitulates key aspects of tuberculosis pathogenesis (Davis et al., 2002).
evidence: This is cited from Davis et al., 2002.

claim: The zebrafish larva's small size and relative permeability to small molecules allow for chemical genetic screening in the context of whole animals.
source: In addition, the zebrafish larva's small size and relative permeability to small molecules allow for chemical genetic screening in the context of whole animals (MacRae and Peterson, 2015).
evidence: This is cited from MacRae and Peterson, 2015.

claim: The 1200 FDA-approved drugs of the Prestwick Chemical Library were screened using zebrafish larvae infected with fluorescent M. marinum.
source: To identify novel host-directed therapies that reduce mycobacterial burden in vivo, we screened the 1200 FDA-approved drugs of the Prestwick Chemical Library using zebrafish larvae infected with fluorescent M. marinum (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is described in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Three animals per well in a 96-well format were each infected with ~ 150 CFU of M. marinum and maintained for 5 days at a 5 µM concentration of each compound.
source: Three animals per well in a 96-well format were each infected with ~ 150 CFU of M. marinum and maintained for 5 days at a 5 µM concentration of each compound.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the screen.

claim: Quantitation of bacterial fluorescence driven by a stable, constitutive promoter provides a validated measure of bacterial burden in zebrafish larvae.
source: Quantitation of bacterial fluorescence driven by a stable, constitutive promoter provides a validated measure of bacterial burden in zebrafish larvae (Adams et al., 2011; Takaki et al., 2013; Walton et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from Adams et al., 2011; Takaki et al., 2013; Walton et al., 2018.

claim: 51 compounds reduced mycobacterial burden in vivo in the initial screen.
source: From the initial screen, we identified 51 compounds that reduced mycobacterial burden in vivo.
evidence: This is a result from the primary screen described in the text.

claim: 23 of the 51 compounds identified resulted in reduced bacterial burdens in a second set of in vivo infections.
source: In a secondary screen of these potential hits, we found that 23 of the 51 compounds identified resulted in reduced bacterial burdens in a second set of in vivo infections, and these 23 compounds were selected for further analysis.
evidence: This is a result from the secondary screen described in the text.

claim: Three compounds exhibited direct anti-mycobacterial activity at the concentrations tested, each previously reported to have antimicrobial activity.
source: Three compounds, each previously reported to have antimicrobial activity, exhibited direct anti-mycobacterial activity at the concentrations tested (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–D), validating our ability to recapitulate the effect of known anti-tubercular drugs in an in vivo model.
evidence: This is supported by the broth culture data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: Sulfamethazine was not effective at 5 µM in broth culture, but was effective in vivo.
source: A known antibiotic, sulfamethazine, was not effective at 5 µM in broth culture, but was effective in vivo, suggesting that in vivo distribution kinetics and/or metabolism may enhance potency.
evidence: This is based on the comparison of in vivo and in vitro results for sulfamethazine.

claim: The whole animal drug screening approach was able to identify antibiotics that are effective in vivo but might be missed in screens of axenic cultures.
source: Thus, the whole animal drug screening approach was able to identify antibiotics that are effective in vivo but might be missed in screens of axenic cultures (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on the sulfamethazine result.

claim: 19 compounds reduced bacterial burden in vivo but not in culture.
source: The 19 compounds that reduced bacterial burden in vivo but not in culture were obtained from independent sources and tested in larger cohorts.
evidence: This is a result from the tertiary screen described in the text.

claim: 9 of the 19 potential host-directed compounds resulted in consistently reduced bacterial burdens in three independent in vivo experiments but had no effect on bacterial growth in liquid broth culture.
source: Of these 19 potential host-directed compounds, 9 resulted in consistently reduced bacterial burdens in three independent in vivo experiments but had no effect on bacterial growth in liquid broth culture (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Prothionamide is a pro-drug that can be metabolized into active anti-mycobacterial forms by both bacteria and host.
source: One of the nine, prothionamide, appeared to be host-dependent at the concentration tested but is likely not host-directed (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1); prothionamide is a pro-drug that can be metabolized into active anti-mycobacterial forms by both bacteria and host (Nishida and Ortiz de Montellano, 2011).
evidence: This is cited from Nishida and Ortiz de Montellano, 2011.

claim: Desipramine had been described previously as a potential HDT and is proposed to act through inhibition of acid sphingomyelinase.
source: Of the remaining eight compounds we identified as likely to be host-directed therapies (Figure 1C–J), one drug, desipramine, had been described previously as a potential HDT; it is proposed to act through inhibition of acid sphingomyelinase, which has been implicated in necroptosis and the response to mycobacterial infection in zebrafish (Roca and Ramakrishnan, 2013).
evidence: This is cited from Roca and Ramakrishnan, 2013.

claim: Chlorpromazine is known to inhibit acid sphingomyelinase, although it also has reported anti-mycobacterial activity in culture.
source: Chlorpromazine is known to inhibit acid sphingomyelinase, although it also has reported anti-mycobacterial activity in culture (Amaral et al., 2007).
evidence: This is cited from Amaral et al., 2007.

claim: Six of the eight compounds identified as likely to be host-directed therapies had not previously been considered as a potential host-directed therapy for mycobacterial infection.
source: To the best of our knowledge, none of the six remaining compounds had previously been considered as a potential host-directed therapy for mycobacterial infection.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the findings based on the authors' knowledge.

claim: Clemastine is an inexpensive, widely available, over-the-counter antihistamine.
source: We chose to focus on the most potent of these, clemastine, an inexpensive, widely available, over-the-counter antihistamine.
evidence: This is a statement about the known properties of clemastine.

claim: Clemastine consistently reduced mycobacterial growth in vivo over the course of a 5-day infection.
source: We found that clemastine consistently reduced mycobacterial growth in vivo over the course of a 5-day infection (Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2A–B.

claim: The effect of clemastine was dose dependent.
source: The effect was dose dependent (Figure 2C), and at a concentration of 5 µM resulted in a ~ 60% reduction in bacterial burden by 5 days post-infection (dpi).
evidence: This is supported by the dose-response data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: At a concentration of 5 µM, clemastine resulted in a ~ 60% reduction in bacterial burden by 5 days post-infection.
source: The effect was dose dependent (Figure 2C), and at a concentration of 5 µM resulted in a ~ 60% reduction in bacterial burden by 5 days post-infection (dpi).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: At 5 dpi, there were fewer total infection foci, and areas of infection were smaller in clemastine-treated animals.
source: At 5 dpi, there were fewer total infection foci, and areas of infection were smaller (Figure 2B), indicating that clemastine reduces bacterial burden significantly after just a few days of infection.
evidence: This is supported by the images shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Clemastine had no effect on bacterial growth in culture conditions at concentrations up to 50 µM.
source: In culture conditions, clemastine had no effect on bacterial growth at concentrations up to 50 µM, although at higher concentrations that were toxic to larvae (100 µM), there was some reduction in bacterial growth in culture (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by the broth culture data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Clemastine functions to reduce bacterial burden in whole animals in a host-dependent manner.
source: Thus, clemastine functions to reduce bacterial burden in whole animals in a host-dependent manner.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of effect in broth culture and the effect in vivo.

claim: Macrophages are central host cells in mycobacterial infection in humans and animal models, including zebrafish.
source: Macrophages are central host cells in mycobacterial infection in humans and animal models, including zebrafish (Clay et al., 2007; Philips and Ernst, 2012).
evidence: This is cited from Clay et al., 2007 and Philips and Ernst, 2012.

claim: Mutations in the gene encoding the myeloid transcription factor Irf8 result in an absence of larval macrophages, due to impaired differentiation from myeloid precursors.
source: Mutations in the gene encoding the myeloid transcription factor Irf8 result in an absence of larval macrophages, due to impaired differentiation from myeloid precursors (Shiau et al., 2015).
evidence: This is cited from Shiau et al., 2015.

claim: In irf8 mutants, bacterial burdens are higher, with extracellular bacterial growth.
source: In irf8 mutants, similar to other macrophage-deficient animals, bacterial burdens are higher, with extracellular bacterial growth (Pagán et al., 2015).
evidence: This is cited from Pagán et al., 2015.

claim: Clemastine was ineffective in irf8-deficient animals.
source: We found that clemastine was ineffective in irf8-deficient animals (Figure 2E–F), suggesting that clemastine's action requires functional macrophages.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2E–F.

claim: Clemastine's action requires functional macrophages.
source: We found that clemastine was ineffective in irf8-deficient animals (Figure 2E–F), suggesting that clemastine's action requires functional macrophages.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of effect in irf8 mutants.

claim: Host mutations that compromise the ability of macrophages to restrict intracellular mycobacterial growth result in higher numbers of bacteria per macrophage.
source: Host mutations that compromise the ability of macrophages to restrict intracellular mycobacterial growth result in higher numbers of bacteria per macrophage, while bacterial mutants attenuated for intracellular growth exhibit reduced bacterial numbers within each macrophage (Takaki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from Takaki et al., 2013.

claim: Clemastine treatment for 24 hours reduced the number of bacteria per macrophage by ~ 30%.
source: Clemastine treatment for 24 hours reduced the number of bacteria per macrophage by ~ 30%, suggesting that clemastine enhances control of mycobacterial infection at the level of individual infected macrophages, even before formation of granulomas (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Clemastine enhances control of mycobacterial infection at the level of individual infected macrophages, even before formation of granulomas.
source: Clemastine treatment for 24 hours reduced the number of bacteria per macrophage by ~ 30%, suggesting that clemastine enhances control of mycobacterial infection at the level of individual infected macrophages, even before formation of granulomas (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is an inference based on the reduction in bacteria per macrophage at 24 hours.

claim: Clemastine did not alter the total number of macrophages per animal.
source: Importantly, clemastine did not alter the total number of macrophages per animal (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Clemastine-treated animals consistently showed loss of bacterial fluorescence within macrophages, while control-treated animals did not.
source: Clemastine-treated animals consistently showed loss of bacterial fluorescence within macrophages, while control-treated animals did not, suggesting that clemastine enhances the microbicidal activity of macrophages (Video 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the live imaging data shown in Video 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Clemastine enhances the microbicidal activity of macrophages.
source: Clemastine-treated animals consistently showed loss of bacterial fluorescence within macrophages, while control-treated animals did not, suggesting that clemastine enhances the microbicidal activity of macrophages (Video 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the loss of bacterial fluorescence in clemastine-treated animals.

claim: Pathogenic mycobacteria can limit acidification of the phagosome, creating a replicative niche within macrophages.
source: Pathogenic mycobacteria can limit acidification of the phagosome, creating a replicative niche within macrophages (Rohde et al., 2007).
evidence: This is cited from Rohde et al., 2007.

claim: Clemastine did not increase the proportion of bacteria that induce the aprA reporter.
source: We measured the ratio of green fluorescence to red fluorescence in M. marinum aprA'::GFP,smyc'::mCherry infections in vivo and observed that clemastine did not increase the proportion of bacteria that induce the aprA reporter (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E), indicating that clemastine likely does not act through increased rates of phagosome acidification.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Clemastine likely does not act through increased rates of phagosome acidification.
source: We measured the ratio of green fluorescence to red fluorescence in M. marinum aprA'::GFP,smyc'::mCherry infections in vivo and observed that clemastine did not increase the proportion of bacteria that induce the aprA reporter (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E), indicating that clemastine likely does not act through increased rates of phagosome acidification.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of change in aprA reporter induction.

claim: P2RX7 is a ligand-gated cation channel activated by extracellular ATP, which is found at sites of infection and injury.
source: P2RX7 is a ligand-gated cation channel activated by extracellular ATP, which is found at sites of infection and injury (Di Virgilio et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from Di Virgilio et al., 2017.

claim: In humans, mice, and fish, P2RX7 is highly expressed on immune cells.
source: In humans, mice, and fish, P2RX7 is highly expressed on immune cells (Di Virgilio et al., 2017; He et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from Di Virgilio et al., 2017 and He et al., 2013.

claim: One cell culture study had reported that clemastine can potentiate human P2X7 receptor (P2RX7) activity.
source: One cell culture study had reported that clemastine can potentiate human P2X7 receptor (P2RX7) activity (Nörenberg et al., 2011).
evidence: This is cited from Nörenberg et al., 2011.

claim: Two different alleles of p2rx7 (p2rx7xt26 and p2rx7xt28) were isolated and outcrossed using CRISPR/Cas9-based targeting.
source: Using CRISPR/Cas9-based targeting, we isolated and outcrossed two different alleles predicted to abolish the second transmembrane domain of zebrafish P2RX7 receptor (P2rx7) (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: This is described in the text and shown in Figure 3A–B.

claim: Both p2rx7 alleles (p2rx7xt26 and p2rx7xt28) result in frameshifts in exon 10 and predicted stop codons upstream of the second transmembrane domain.
source: Both alleles (p2rx7xt26 and p2rx7xt28) result in frameshifts in exon 10 and predicted stop codons upstream of the second transmembrane domain, suggesting that both alleles are functional nulls (Smart et al., 2003).
evidence: This is described in the text and shown in Figure 3B, with citation to Smart et al., 2003.

claim: Both p2rx7 alleles are functional nulls.
source: Both alleles (p2rx7xt26 and p2rx7xt28) result in frameshifts in exon 10 and predicted stop codons upstream of the second transmembrane domain, suggesting that both alleles are functional nulls (Smart et al., 2003).
evidence: This is an inference based on the predicted protein structure changes.

claim: Both infected and uninfected macrophages in the caudal area underwent stereotypical calcium flashes at ~ 0.1 flashes per minute.
source: We found that both infected and uninfected macrophages in the caudal area underwent stereotypical calcium flashes (Figure 3C–D) at ~ 0.1 flashes per minute (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, Video 2).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3C–D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, and Video 2.

claim: Administration of clemastine significantly enhanced the frequency of macrophage calcium transients more than two-fold in infected cells.
source: Administration of clemastine significantly enhanced the frequency of these macrophage calcium transients more than two-fold in infected cells (Figure 3C and Video 3).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3C and Video 3.

claim: Clemastine increased the frequency of calcium transients more than two-fold in infected wildtype animals, but this effect was abrogated in p2rx7 mutants.
source: In infected wildtype animals, clemastine increased the frequency of calcium transients more than two-fold, but this effect was abrogated in p2rx7 mutants (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Clemastine did not significantly increase calcium transients in uninfected cells in infected fish.
source: Clemastine did not significantly increase calcium transients in uninfected cells in infected fish (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Clemastine's enhancement of calcium transients in Mycobacterium-infected cells may occur through potentiation, rather than direct agonism of P2rx7.
source: Thus, clemastine's enhancement of calcium transients in Mycobacterium-infected cells may occur through potentiation, rather than direct agonism of P2rx7.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of effect in uninfected cells.

claim: p2rx7 mutants did not show significant differences in overall bacterial burden, although there was a slight decrease in bacterial burden in p2rx7 mutants.
source: p2rx7 mutants did not show significant differences in overall bacterial burden, although there was a slight decrease in bacterial burden in p2rx7 mutants (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Clemastine consistently reduced burden in wildtype animals but failed to reduce bacterial burden in p2rx7 mutants.
source: Clemastine consistently reduced burden in wildtype animals but failed to reduce bacterial burden in p2rx7 mutants (Figure 4A–B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 4A–B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: Both the altered macrophage calcium dynamics and reduction in bacterial burden were dependent on functional P2rx7.
source: Thus, both the altered macrophage calcium dynamics and reduction in bacterial burden were dependent on functional P2rx7.
evidence: This is an inference based on the results in p2rx7 mutants.

claim: P2RX7 signaling has been shown to promote inflammasome activation.
source: P2RX7 signaling has been shown to promote inflammasome activation (Fairbairn et al., 2001; Piccini et al., 2008), which can result in killing of intracellular pathogens (Ferrari et al., 2006; Franceschini et al., 2015; Moreira-Souza et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from Fairbairn et al., 2001; Piccini et al., 2008; Ferrari et al., 2006; Franceschini et al., 2015; Moreira-Souza et al., 2017.

claim: Activation of inflammasomes is dependent on cytosolic sensing of PAMPs or DAMPs.
source: Activation of inflammasomes is dependent on cytosolic sensing of PAMPs or DAMPs (Lamkanfi and Dixit, 2014).
evidence: This is cited from Lamkanfi and Dixit, 2014.

claim: Pathogenic mycobacteria secrete a variety of effector proteins that access the host cytosol, presumably through permeabilization of the phagosomal membrane.
source: Pathogenic mycobacteria secrete a variety of effector proteins that access the host cytosol, presumably through permeabilization of the phagosomal membrane; cytosolic access is dependent on the specialized secretion system ESX-1 (Conrad et al., 2017; Koo et al., 2008; Manzanillo et al., 2012; Wassermann et al., 2015).
evidence: This is cited from Conrad et al., 2017; Koo et al., 2008; Manzanillo et al., 2012; Wassermann et al., 2015.

claim: Mycobacteria lacking the RD1 region, which encompasses the ESX-1 type VII secretion system, fail to engage cytosol-based host responses.
source: Mycobacteria lacking the RD1 region, which encompasses the ESX-1 type VII secretion system, fail to engage cytosol-based host responses (Abdallah et al., 2011; Dorhoi et al., 2012; Volkman et al., 2004).
evidence: This is cited from Abdallah et al., 2011; Dorhoi et al., 2012; Volkman et al., 2004.

claim: Clemastine had no effect on burden in the ∆RD1 mutants.
source: In contrast to its effect on wildtype M. marinum, clemastine had no effect on burden in the ∆RD1 mutants (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: M. marinum transposon mutants in the gene cmaA2 were attenuated in the zebrafish model.
source: We found that M. marinum transposon mutants in the gene cmaA2, which encodes a trans-cyclopropane synthetase (Glickman et al., 2001), were attenuated in the zebrafish model.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, with citation to Glickman et al., 2001.

claim: Clemastine was able to reduce bacterial load in cmaA2 mutant infections despite a burden comparable to the ∆RD1 mutants.
source: Despite a burden comparable to the ∆RD1 mutants (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), clemastine still was able to reduce bacterial load, suggesting that the RD1-dependent effect was not merely due to differences in burden.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: When the inoculum of ∆RD1 mutant bacteria was increased above wildtype levels, clemastine is still ineffective.
source: Reciprocally, when we increased the inoculum of ∆RD1 mutant bacteria above wildtype levels, clemastine is still ineffective (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: During the first 24 hr of infection, clemastine reduced the number of WT bacteria per macrophage but failed to reduce the number of bacteria per macrophage in the ∆RD1 infection.
source: Additionally, we examined early control of bacterial growth in ∆RD1 infections. During the first 24 hr of infection, clemastine reduced the number of WT bacteria per macrophage (Figure 2G and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D) but failed to reduce the number of bacteria per macrophage in the ∆RD1 infection (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2G and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Clemastine efficacy requires a host defense pathway dependent on cytosolic engagement, regardless of bacterial load.
source: These data are consistent with a model in which clemastine efficacy requires a host defense pathway dependent on cytosolic engagement, regardless of bacterial load.
evidence: This is an inference based on the ∆RD1 and cmaA2 mutant results.

claim: ASC is required for inflammasome assembly in humans, mice, and zebrafish.
source: We focused on the common adaptor ASC, which is required for inflammasome assembly in humans, mice, and zebrafish (Kuri et al., 2017; Lamkanfi and Dixit, 2014).
evidence: This is cited from Kuri et al., 2017 and Lamkanfi and Dixit, 2014.

claim: A 14 base pair deletion allele, pycardw216, was generated in the first exon of the zebrafish asc orthologue using TALEN technology.
source: We generated asc mutant zebrafish (zebrafish gene name pycard) using TALEN technology and generated a 14 base pair deletion allele, pycardw216, in the first exon of the zebrafish asc orthologue (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A), resulting in a premature stop codon.
evidence: This is described in the text and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: ASC-deficient animals do not exhibit dramatically increased susceptibility to mycobacterial infection.
source: As in mice, ASC-deficient animals do not exhibit dramatically increased susceptibility to mycobacterial infection (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Clemastine reduced burden in wildtype and heterozygous sibling control animals, but was completely ineffective in zebrafish asc mutants.
source: However, while clemastine reduced burden in wildtype and heterozygous sibling control animals, it was completely ineffective in zebrafish asc mutants (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 2B–C).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B–C.

claim: Inflammasome activation may be limited during infection with pathogenic mycobacteria, but enhancement can lead to increased bacterial killing.
source: These results are consistent with a model in which inflammasome activation may be limited during infection with pathogenic mycobacteria, but enhancement can lead to increased bacterial killing.
evidence: This is an inference based on the asc mutant results.

claim: Clemastine treatment does not enhance the number or frequency of LC3-decorated mycobacteria over the course of three days of infection.
source: Using spinning disk confocal microscopy, we observed that clemastine treatment does not enhance the number or frequency of LC3-decorated mycobacteria over the course of three days of infection (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Autophagy is not the host-directed mechanism through which clemastine reduces bacterial burden in vivo.
source: These findings are in agreement with the observed lack of change in acidification of mycobacteria, suggesting that autophagy is not the host-directed mechanism through which clemastine reduces bacterial burden in vivo.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of change in LC3 decoration and acidification.

claim: Adult zebrafish granulomas share key features with human Mtb granulomas, including a caseous necrotic core and a tight epithelialized layer.
source: Adult zebrafish granulomas share key features with human Mtb granulomas, including a caseous necrotic core and a tight epithelialized layer that alters bacterial physiology and may restrict access to drugs (Cronan et al., 2016; Lenaerts et al., 2015; Swaim et al., 2006).
evidence: This is cited from Cronan et al., 2016; Lenaerts et al., 2015; Swaim et al., 2006.

claim: Upon multi-day (5–7 days) treatment with clemastine, there was a nearly 70% reduction in mycobacterial fluorescence relative to vehicle control granulomas.
source: Upon multi-day (5–7 days) treatment with clemastine, we found a nearly 70% reduction in mycobacterial fluorescence relative to vehicle control granulomas, suggesting that clemastine has efficacy both in established infections (>2 weeks post infection) and in the context of a mature granuloma (Figure 6A–B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6A–B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: Clemastine has efficacy both in established infections (>2 weeks post infection) and in the context of a mature granuloma.
source: Upon multi-day (5–7 days) treatment with clemastine, we found a nearly 70% reduction in mycobacterial fluorescence relative to vehicle control granulomas, suggesting that clemastine has efficacy both in established infections (>2 weeks post infection) and in the context of a mature granuloma (Figure 6A–B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is an inference based on the granuloma explant results.

claim: Clemastine treatment significantly increased the percentage of cells positive for FLICA relative to the DMSO control.
source: Using this tool and flow-cytometry methods developed for Myco-GEM (Cronan et al., 2018), we found that clemastine treatment significantly increased the percentage of cells positive for FLICA relative to the DMSO control (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: Clemastine-treated granulomas had a nearly 10-fold reduction in luminescence relative to control granulomas after 6 days of treatment.
source: Clemastine-treated granulomas had a nearly 10-fold reduction in luminescence relative to control granulomas after 6 days of treatment (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 3A), suggesting that the effect size may be greater than that observed by fluorescence-based readouts.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Clemastine treatment significantly reduced CFU by ~ 1.4 log10 (~ 27 fold) compared to vehicle-exposed granulomas after a week of Myco-GEM culture.
source: We found that clemastine treatment significantly reduced CFU by ~ 1.4 log10 (~ 27 fold) compared to vehicle-exposed granulomas after a week of Myco-GEM culture (Figure 6E, Figure 6—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Clemastine treatment significantly enhanced the effect of moxifloxacin in Myco-GEM granulomas.
source: Clemastine treatment significantly enhanced the effect of moxifloxacin in Myco-GEM granulomas (Figure 6F, Figure 6—figure supplement 3C), suggesting that it can act as a combination host-directed therapy with other antibiotics in the context of a complex, established infection.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Clemastine can act as a combination host-directed therapy with other antibiotics in the context of a complex, established infection.
source: Clemastine treatment significantly enhanced the effect of moxifloxacin in Myco-GEM granulomas (Figure 6F, Figure 6—figure supplement 3C), suggesting that it can act as a combination host-directed therapy with other antibiotics in the context of a complex, established infection.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combination treatment results.

claim: Multi-drug resistant TB strains were responsible for an estimated 480,000 new TB cases in 2014, with an estimated treatment failure rate of 46%.
source: Multi-drug resistant strains (which require 9–24 months of treatment, including use of an injectable agent) were responsible for an estimated 480,000 new TB cases in 2014, with an estimated treatment failure rate of 46% (World Health Organization, 2018).
evidence: This is cited from the World Health Organization 2018 report.

claim: Large drug screens in whole animals would be extremely challenging in other vertebrates.
source: Large drug screens in whole animals would be extremely challenging in other vertebrates, but the small size, relative permeability, and fecundity of zebrafish enable high-throughput chemical screens.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of zebrafish for drug screening.

claim: The small size, relative permeability, and fecundity of zebrafish enable high-throughput chemical screens.
source: Large drug screens in whole animals would be extremely challenging in other vertebrates, but the small size, relative permeability, and fecundity of zebrafish enable high-throughput chemical screens.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of zebrafish for drug screening.

claim: The frequency of calcium transients in zebrafish macrophages is similar to what has been reported for infected Drosophila macrophages in vivo.
source: Interestingly, the frequency of calcium transients in zebrafish macrophages is similar to what has been reported for infected Drosophila macrophages in vivo (Weavers et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from Weavers et al., 2016.

claim: P2RX7 activation has been implicated in a variety of inflammatory and immune processes.
source: We identified an important moonlighting activity for clemastine in mycobacterial infection: potentiation of the purinergic receptor, P2RX7. That target, P2RX7, has been implicated in a variety of inflammatory and immune processes; its activation can result in bacterial killing in cell culture (Coutinho-Silva et al., 2003; Fairbairn et al., 2001; Santos et al., 2013) (reviewed in Di Virgilio et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from Coutinho-Silva et al., 2003; Fairbairn et al., 2001; Santos et al., 2013; Di Virgilio et al., 2017.

claim: P2RX7 activation can result in bacterial killing in cell culture.
source: We identified an important moonlighting activity for clemastine in mycobacterial infection: potentiation of the purinergic receptor, P2RX7. That target, P2RX7, has been implicated in a variety of inflammatory and immune processes; its activation can result in bacterial killing in cell culture (Coutinho-Silva et al., 2003; Fairbairn et al., 2001; Santos et al., 2013) (reviewed in Di Virgilio et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from Coutinho-Silva et al., 2003; Fairbairn et al., 2001; Santos et al., 2013.

claim: Polymorphisms in the P2RX7 receptor have been associated with TB susceptibility in humans.
source: Intriguingly, polymorphisms in the P2RX7 receptor have been associated with TB susceptibility in humans (Li et al., 2002; Wu et al., 2014) and functional changes contribute to TB pathogenesis in some cell culture models but have given divergent results in different mouse models (Amaral et al., 2014; Myers et al., 2005; Santos et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from Li et al., 2002 and Wu et al., 2014.

claim: In cell culture, P2RX7 activation enhances mycobacterial killing in an ATP-dependent manner.
source: In cell culture, P2RX7 activation enhances mycobacterial killing in an ATP-dependent manner (Placido et al., 2006), and these findings are consistent with our in vivo data with clemastine and P2RX7 activation.
evidence: This is cited from Placido et al., 2006.

claim: Direct potentiation of the P2RX7 channel enhances host control of infection.
source: Here, however, the in vivo drug screen uncovered a novel approach to modulating P2RX7 during mycobacterial infection. While previous studies have focused on the effects of loss of function of P2RX7, we show that direct potentiation of the channel enhances host control of infection.
evidence: This is supported by the data showing clemastine's effect on infection in vivo.

claim: Potentiation of an ATP-responsive channel rather than constitutive activation represents a more nuanced approach to enhancing the host immune response and may avoid problems associated with excessive or inappropriate macrophage activation.
source: Potentiation of an ATP-responsive channel rather than constitutive activation thus represents a more nuanced approach to enhancing the host immune response and may avoid problems associated with excessive or inappropriate macrophage activation (Feng et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential advantages of potentiation, with citation to Feng et al., 2016.

claim: Only infected cells exhibited increased calcium transients during clemastine treatment.
source: Supporting the notion of a localized and infection-specific effect of the drug, only infected cells exhibited increased calcium transients during clemastine treatment.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: P2RX7 activation has been strongly linked to inflammasome activation.
source: P2RX7 activation has been strongly linked to inflammasome activation (Di Virgilio, 2007), but there is divergent evidence for the precise roles of inflammasome signaling during mycobacterial infection (Briken et al., 2013; Mayer-Barber et al., 2010).
evidence: This is cited from Di Virgilio, 2007; Briken et al., 2013; Mayer-Barber et al., 2010.

claim: In mycobacterial mutants lacking ESX-1, there is a drastic reduction in IL-1B production in vitro, with effects on the AIM2 inflammasome.
source: In mycobacterial mutants lacking ESX-1, there is a drastic reduction in IL-1B production in vitro, with effects on the AIM2 inflammasome (Wassermann et al., 2015).
evidence: This is cited from Wassermann et al., 2015.

claim: Non-virulent mycobacteria increase inflammasome activation compared to virulent strains.
source: Others have shown that non-virulent mycobacteria increase inflammasome activation compared to virulent strains (Shah et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from Shah et al., 2013.

claim: Zebrafish asc larvae had no significant differences in mycobacterial burden.
source: Consistent with findings in mice, the zebrafish asc larvae had no significant differences in mycobacterial burden (Mayer-Barber et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5B, with citation to Mayer-Barber et al., 2010.

claim: Mutations in other key inflammasome genes enhance susceptibility to mycobacterial infections in animal models.
source: However, mutations in other key inflammasome genes enhance susceptibility to mycobacterial infections in animal models, indicating that inflammasomes can be involved in host protection (Fremond et al., 2007; Juffermans et al., 2000).
evidence: This is cited from Fremond et al., 2007 and Juffermans et al., 2000.

claim: Clemastine is completely ineffective in inflammasome-deficient animals.
source: Notably, we show that clemastine is completely ineffective in inflammasome-deficient animals, supporting a model in which inflammasome signaling can be host-beneficial.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Inflammasome activation through P2rx7 potentiation may enhance mycobacterial killing, potentially by overcoming bacterially mediated inhibition.
source: Thus, inflammasome activation through P2rx7 potentiation may enhance mycobacterial killing, potentially by overcoming bacterially mediated inhibition.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the results.

claim: Excess stimulation of inflammasome signaling has been shown to be host-detrimental.
source: While excess stimulation of inflammasome signaling has also been shown to be host-detrimental (Mishra et al., 2013), there may be differences between a more nuanced and localized potentiation of the P2RX7 response to ATP and more general enhancement of inflammasome activation.
evidence: This is cited from Mishra et al., 2013.

claim: Clemastine recently showed promise in a clinical trial for patients with multiple sclerosis.
source: Clemastine recently showed promise in a clinical trial for patients with multiple sclerosis (Green et al., 2017), and – due to its safety profile – would be a prime candidate for low-risk/high-reward studies in humans.
evidence: This is cited from Green et al., 2017.

claim: Clemastine is effective both in early infections in zebrafish larvae and in longer term, established infections.
source: Clemastine is effective both in early infections in zebrafish larvae and in longer term, established infections.
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figures 2 and 6.

claim: Clemastine reduces intracellular bacterial burden through potentiation of the purinergic receptor P2rx7 to induce inflammasome activation in both nascent and established mycobacterial infections.
source: Taken together, these data suggest a model (Figure 7) in which clemastine reduces intracellular bacterial burden through potentiation of the purinergic receptor P2rx7 to induce inflammasome activation in both nascent and established mycobacterial infections.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings presented in the manuscript, shown in Figure 7.

claim: Modulation of a P2RX7 inflammasome axis is a promising avenue for host-directed therapies against mycobacterial infection in established disease.
source: Thus, modulation of a P2RX7 inflammasome axis is a promising avenue for host-directed therapies against mycobacterial infection in established disease.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the findings of the study.

claim: Clemastine's mechanism of action was unlikely to be attributable to its antihistamine activity.
source: Clemastine's mechanism of action was unlikely to be attributable to its antihistamine activity. Of the 41 antihistamines in the Prestwick Chemical Library, only one other in a separate class, trimeprazine, was identified as a hit. In addition, diphenhydramine, another antihistamine of the same family as clemastine, had no effect on bacterial burden (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of effect of other antihistamines.

claim: Of the 41 antihistamines in the Prestwick Chemical Library, only one other in a separate class, trimeprazine, was identified as a hit.
source: Of the 41 antihistamines in the Prestwick Chemical Library, only one other in a separate class, trimeprazine, was identified as a hit.
evidence: This is a result from the screen.

claim: Diphenhydramine, another antihistamine of the same family as clemastine, had no effect on bacterial burden.
source: In addition, diphenhydramine, another antihistamine of the same family as clemastine, had no effect on bacterial burden (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Calcium dynamics during mycobacterial infection have not been assessed in vertebrate models in vivo prior to this study.
source: Although calcium dynamics during mycobacterial infection have previously been studied in cultured macrophages, they have not been assessed in vertebrate models in vivo.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the approach.

claim: Clemastine is ineffective against ∆RD1 mutant bacteria regardless of bacterial load.
source: Reciprocally, when we increased the inoculum of ∆RD1 mutant bacteria above wildtype levels, clemastine is still ineffective (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B). This was true using independent measures of bacterial burden at five dpi including fluorescence (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) and 16S rRNA-based measures of burden (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing no effect at different bacterial loads.

claim: The Prestwick Chemical Library contains additional antimycobacterial agents that did not emerge as hits.
source: The Prestwick Chemical Library contains additional antimycobacterial agents that did not emerge as hits; however, a number of these compounds are ineffective in zebrafish larvae at the 5 µM concentration used during our screen (Adams et al., 2011; Takaki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from Adams et al., 2011 and Takaki et al., 2013.

claim: Moxifloxacin has reduced effectiveness against mycobacteria in cultured granulomas relative to mycobacteria cultured in vitro.
source: We have previously found that moxifloxacin has reduced effectiveness against mycobacteria in cultured granulomas relative to mycobacteria cultured in vitro (Cronan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from Cronan et al., 2018.

claim: Homozygous p2rx7 mutants were viable and exhibited no apparent anatomical or fertility defects.
source: Homozygous p2rx7 mutants were viable and exhibited no apparent anatomical or fertility defects.
evidence: This is an observation from the generation of the mutant line.

claim: pycard mutant animals are viable as adults and of similar size and fecundity.
source: pycard mutant animals are viable as adults and of similar size and fecundity.
evidence: This is an observation from the generation of the mutant line.
